answer: A bonded-identity rule resists sybils: each agent must lock stake for a full epoch before its vote counts, and its record is tied to a hardware key so clones start at zero. An operator minting a thousand fakes pays the bond and upkeep on all of them, so cost scales linearly in real money, unlike a free nectar spill. Clones sharing one seed merge into a single voice, leaving no pigment of fake diversity in tallies. If a swing address fakes a comet of chatter, the checkpoint slashes the lock. Faking consensus costs more than honest mining.
